subject: Quarterly netting & invoice origin delegation
messages:
From: Lisa Nguyen <lisa@ecom-retail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Apex Payments <apex-payments@apexpayments.com>
Date: 2028-08-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quarterly netting & invoice origin delegation

Hi Ben —

We’re preparing the AP process for Q3 and exploring whether Redwood can support a quarterly netting approach for our account. We currently receive invoices from multiple Redwood billing entities (EU/UK/US) and our treasury team would like one consolidated netted invoice/statement for payments on a quarterly cadence. A few questions to start:

- Can Redwood issue a single quarterly netted invoice/statement that aggregates charges across entities and shows the net amount due?
- If yes, which entity would be the invoice originator on that consolidated document (Redwood entity or E‑Com Retail entity)?
- Does opting into a consolidated/quarterly netting flow require portal enrollment, or can we keep receiving PDF invoices by email (we typically need an emailed copy for our AR system)?
- Any special VAT/tax evidence you need from us to make this work across EU entities?

Attached a sample of how our AP team prefers netting disclosures and an example invoice for reference.

Billing contact for this work is payments+ecom@ecom-retail.com — please copy them on next steps.

Thanks,
Lisa Nguyen
Head of Treasury, E‑Com Retail

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Nguyen <lisa@ecom-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Apex Payments <apex-payments@apexpayments.com>
Date: 2028-08-01T12:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Quarterly netting & invoice origin delegation

Hi Lisa —

Thanks — good, concrete questions. I discussed this with Billing & Ops and summarised viable approaches below. Short answer: we can support consolidated netting, but there are tradeoffs depending on whether you want a single legal originator or a consolidated statement with entity-level VAT detail.

Options (pros/cons):

1) Portal-native consolidated statement (recommended)
   - Redwood publishes a single quarterly statement in the customer portal that nets across entities.
   - We also provide per-entity VAT breakdowns and downloadable PDFs for your AP system.
   - Pros: single canonical record, audit trail, easy corrections; supports automated pulls via webhook.
   - Cons: requires portal enrollment for canonical statement (we can still email copies).

2) Email-only consolidated PDF from Redwood
   - We can generate a consolidated PDF and email it to payments+ecom@ecom-retail.com monthly/quarterly.
   - Pros: minimal changes on your side.
   - Cons: PDFs are not as robust for automatic reconciliation and we can’t attach per-entity VAT-certified stubs inline (we can include them as extra attachments).

3) Delegated invoice originator (entity mapping)
   - If you prefer the netted invoice to show a specific Redwood legal entity as originator, we can map charges to that originator for the consolidated document. VAT treatment will depend on which legal entity issues the invoice.

Required next steps from E‑Com to proceed:
- Confirm whether you want portal enrollment (recommended) or email-only delivery.
- Confirm the billing contact (you already provided payments+ecom@ecom-retail.com — noted).
- Provide VAT IDs for each E‑Com legal entity to be included in the per-entity breakdown.
- Sign the attached master billing agreement and return the AP questions spreadsheet so our ops team can validate remittance instructions.

I attached a short checklist and the master billing agreement for signature. If helpful I can schedule a 30‑minute call with Billing Ops to walk through the VAT flows and file formats we’ll provide.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quarterly netting & invoice origin delegation — VAT/tax checklist

Hi Lisa / Ben —

Looping in from Billing Ops with the tax checklist and a suggested delivery pattern that preserves VAT compliance while giving you a single netted statement for payments. Key points: 

- VAT evidence & per‑entity requirements:
  * For intra‑EU supplies, we need each E‑Com entity’s VAT registration number to populate per‑entity stubs. Those stubs will be included as appendices to the consolidated statement (PDF + portal).
  * If the consolidated statement lists a Redwood legal entity as originator, the VAT rates and invoice numbering will follow that entity’s rules; this may affect how your AP records reverse‑charge entries.

- Recommended final format (compliance + convenience):
  1) Canonical consolidated statement in Portal (single net amount, statement summary).
  2) Attached per‑entity VAT stub PDFs (one per E‑Com legal entity) packaged with the statement.
  3) Email copy of the statement+stubs to payments+ecom@ecom-retail.com when published.

- Documents required from E‑Com to onboard:
  - Spreadsheet with legal entity name, invoice remit-to, VAT ID, and local invoice contact (CSV/XLSX).
  - Confirmation of the remittance bank details (IBAN/BIC when applicable).
  - Signed master billing agreement (we have the draft attached from Ben).

- Timeline & operational notes:
  * If you enroll in the portal this week, we can complete AP mapping and run a dry‑run statement by 2028-09-20 to validate VAT stubs formatting before the Q4 go‑live.
  * There is no need for W‑8/W‑9 for EU entities; those are US tax forms. If you have US-based entities paying Redwood US, we’ll request the appropriate US tax forms separately.

Action items for Lisa / Apex Payments:
- Provide the entity spreadsheet and remit details to billing-ops@redwood.ai.
- Confirm portal enrollment and whether you need monthly vs quarterly cadence (we’ve noted quarterly pilot).

I’ll slot a 30‑minute billing ops walkthrough for next week unless you prefer a different cadence.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
